content: Disabling Windows Defender via third-party tooling is high-risk: tamper protection exists specifically to block unauthorized changes, third-party 'Defender Remover' scripts carry malware/BSOD risk, and disabling real-time protection materially increases infection risk. Recommended alternative for performance concerns is exclusions rather than full disable. Two-phase disable (tamper protection off, then real-time protection off) reflects the actual OS-enforced gate, so a tool must both surface the tamper-protection prerequisite and warn about consequences at each phase.
